In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
osteosarcoma, a malignant neoplasm of the bones, is the most common primary bone malignancy of the skeleton.

osteosarcomas are malignant tumors of bone that are derived from mesenchymal stem cells and are characterized by a high mitotic index, necrosis, and a high rate of local recurrence and distant metastases.

the use of chemotherapy in osteosarcoma patients has improved survival, but it has not been proven that the combination of chemotherapy, surgery and radiotherapy is superior to surgery alone in terms of survival, and the optimal chemotherapy regimen has not been determined.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the majority of patients with osteosarcoma have an excellent prognosis.
we have identified a new mechanism of resistance to chemotherapy and that it is a mechanism that is likely to be relevant to a number of other cancers.
osteosarcoma has a poor prognosis in the pediatric population and that the prognosis is better in the adolescent population.

we need to be more aggressive in treating osteosarcoma in dogs.
